edition.alertText: Third tanker hit by mine Oct 19; Araghchi offers 7-day reopening timeline; Gulf crude flows crash to 8.5M b/d — 50% of pre-war

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis entered day 233 with attacks intensifying to wartime highs. The IRGC claimed on October 19 that a third oil tanker hit a naval mine and caught fire — following claims on October 18 that two laden supertankers each carrying roughly 2 million barrels struck mines in the strait's southern passage. CENTCOM disputes the mine claims, saying vessels were hit by guided projectiles and drones. UKMTO recorded 12 confirmed attacks in the week of October 5–11 — the highest weekly total since the war began — and issued 29 warnings in October to date. The agency said most vessels now refuse to report being hit, so true attack numbers are likely higher. Kpler data shows Gulf crude exports collapsed to approximately 8.5 million barrels per day for the most recent week, down sharply from 11.6 million bpd the prior week — roughly 50% of the 17.1 million bpd pre-war baseline. Daily throughput remains wildly volatile, swinging from 20.8 million barrels on October 8 to 2.9 million on October 11.

Oil markets remain volatile as the conflict's risk premium holds firm. Brent traded near $109.91 on Tuesday, down from last week's $110 touch but still well above pre-war levels of ~$72. WTI dropped below $99 after Trump moved to waive certain Russia energy sanctions and tariffs to ease fuel prices, widening the Brent-WTI spread to over $11 versus a pre-war range of $3–5. VLCC tanker rates remain near $1.3 million per day — 43 times the January level — with freight now making up more than 27% of delivered crude cost versus 3% pre-war. War-risk insurance has risen approximately 30 times pre-crisis levels. The IRGC escalated threats beyond shipping, warning it would target undersea internet cables beneath the strait. Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority added 122 vessels to a non-conformity list for violating transit rules.

Diplomatic channels multiplied but a breakthrough remains elusive. Foreign Minister Araghchi offered a 7-day reopening timeline at the OIC meeting in Baghdad — strait reopens day six, talks resume day seven — but Washington insists any deal address Iran's nuclear programme. Pakistan's army chief Gen. Asim Munir heads to Tehran on Tuesday to push renewed mediation. Russia's Lavrov visited Tehran and proposed a regional collective security architecture, while the GCC urged Moscow to press Iran for dialogue. Iran's nuclear debate intensified, with a senior parliamentary official saying the new Supreme Leader could issue a ruling authorizing weapons development. On supply chains, S&P Global Institute warned on October 19 that Hormuz energy shocks combined with El Niño risks are creating conditions for a global food crisis: fertilizer shipments remain near zero, urea exports are down 83% from pre-war (ITC), Bangladesh has shut four of five urea plants due to LNG shortages, and QatarEnergy has extended LNG force majeure into November.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 45% from pre-war. Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — record highs. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. MEG supplied ~35% of global urea and 25% of ammonia.

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Urea exports down 83%, ammonia down 75% vs pre-war (ITC data). Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz remain near zero. Bangladesh shut 4 of 5 urea plants due to LNG shortages. S&P Global warns of global food crisis as El Niño compounds supply shock. UN fertilizer plan stalled.

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: Qatar LNG exports down 95% from pre-war (ITC). QatarEnergy extended force majeure into November. Europe 12-14% LNG was Qatar. Japan's top LNG buyer sees disruption persisting into winter. Asian buyers switching to coal — Newcastle near $151/t.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint.
